correctness.rationale: The exact derivative πB_e′=(1+e cos f)f sin f(1−eT(f)) holds on (0,π), and T(f)=2 sin(f)/f−3 cos f has one strict maximum by G=(3f²−2)sin f+2f cos f and a one-sign-change derivative. The fold eccentricity is 1/max T≈0.324898008977667, strictly below 1/3; for e between fold and 1/3 interior extrema are local max then min, while full phase is a local max. Envelope differentiation of log(B_e(f_minus)/(1−e)²) gives 2(1+cos f_minus)/[(1−e)(1+e cos f_minus)]>0, and opposite endpoint height signs force one global brightness exchange e≈0.325836262906186, plus a square-root fold. At e=1/3 apastron is a degenerate minimum; full orbit reflection yields the asserted maxima count. Independent derivative and bisection checks corroborate but do not prove universality.
